about.title: About Stepback
about.intro: None of us decides when we leave this world. But stepping back from an avoidable hazard is something we can do today.
about.quote: Nothing happening is the biggest win. Even when the other person made the mistake, getting out of the way and having nothing happen beats an insurance claim or an excuse to rest. Every time.

items.def: The source of potential harm. A truck's right-side blind spot, a wet tile floor, a stopped vehicle in a live lane.
The state that puts you in its path. Standing within 1 m of the truck's side; glancing at your phone in the fast lane.
Severity × likelihood. You rarely get to remove the hazard, but breaking the exposure is a choice you can make. That is why the key field in every case is "Avoidance".

sections.h: Economics: everyone ends up better off
p: In some cafés there are vouchers pinned to the wall. A customer pays a little extra and a voucher goes up; a student takes one down and eats for free. The owner gets business, the giver gets joy, the student gets a meal. Nobody loses and everybody gains a little. Naples' caffè sospeso and Korea's Mirinae shops run on the same principle.

Here, the person who records a close call sees how many people took the lesson. The person it protected pins a ticket with a note and may pledge to a safety fund. The person who takes the ticket gets the lesson and the note. Pledges go back out as avoiding tools: reflective strips, grab bars, rear warning lights.

It matters that a ticket is one-time. A like copies forever and hands nothing to anyone. A ticket can be taken by exactly one person, and once it is gone you feel like pinning one for the next person. That small device is what creates reciprocity.

Aviation cut its accident rate dramatically. One reason is confidential, non-punitive near-miss reporting. A pilot can report "I nearly entered the wrong runway today" without punishment, so reports pile up, and piled-up reports change the system. Heinrich's ratio (1 serious injury : 29 minor : 300 near misses) says the same thing: to prevent the big one, collect the near misses.

So Stepback does not blame. You never have to name the driver, the victim or the place. We record structures, not people. "That driver was reckless" protects nobody. "Next to a turning truck, take one step back" protects someone.
The other lever is social proof. "17 people have taken this lesson" makes the norm visible, so the safe move reads as normal instead of fussy.

sections.h: What spreads is an action, not fear
p: Crash footage spreads as fear, and fear does not change behaviour. Stepback's unit of sharing is one sentence of avoiding action. One card, one sentence, one link. It travels only if the reader can do it tomorrow.

sections.h: What you can do right now
steps: Read one case and press "I take this lesson".
If a lesson has protected you, pin a ticket on the wall.
If you have had a close call, record it. Three fields are enough: the source, the state, the avoiding action.
